summary: Forest Service stone shelter (1908) and permanent lookout (about 1912) on Hahns Peak; off line after WWII, restored 2014-2017, now a popular hike.

facts.design: Stone shelter built 1908; permanent lookout about four years later; enlarged and modernized circa 1942

access.note: Forest Service calls it a popular day hike; Colorado Preservation says it stays accessible to the visitors who hike to it each year.

visit.trail_note: Hike that starts at a lower trailhead; a 2021 visitor walked up the stairs of the lookout.

events.note: Stone shelter built by the Forest Service on the summit.
Permanent cement lookout built about four years after the stone shelter; Historic Routt County gives the span 1908-1912.
Enlarged and modernized circa 1942; served as an Aircraft Warning Service site during World War II.
Date registered September 1, 1997 per the NHLR detail page.
Listed by Colorado Preservation as one of Colorado’s Most Endangered Places.
Colorado Preservation says the site was officially declared “Saved”.
Restoration of the building and hiking trail completed; work by Historic Routt County, the Forest Service, HistoriCorps and Rocky Mountain Youth Corps ran 2014-2017.
Vandalism around July 4 broke multiple windows and badly damaged the entrance door.
HistoriCorps completed repairs after the 2018 vandalism.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 10,759 ft (3,279 m); the Forest Service release and Colorado Preservation give 10,839 ft (about 3,304 m). The story reports both. The brief's NHLR-based value is left for the editor to decide.

Historic Routt County and Colorado Preservation give 1908-1912. NHLR and the Forest Service date the stone shelter to 1908 and the permanent lookout about four years later, so the record uses 1908 and about 1912.

Historic Routt County dates decommissioning to the late 1940s and early 1950s. The Forest Service ties the end of staffing to after World War II and a drop in use in the late 1940s. No exact year is recorded, so no staffed_last event is given.

Colorado Preservation dates the official Saved declaration to 2016. The Forest Service dates completion of the building and trail restoration to 2017, and Historic Routt County lists the project status as Complete 2017.

notes_for_editor: Core history (1908 stone shelter, 1933 damage, 1939 rebuild, c.1942 enlargement, 2014-2017 restoration, 2018 vandalism) is consistent across the NHLR, Forest Service, Historic Routt County and Colorado Preservation pages. Open points: the NHLR elevation (10,759 ft) differs from the 10,839 ft given by the agency and two other sources; the exact year staffing ended is not recorded; the History Colorado page (which gives about 1947) returned no text when fetched, so it is not used. The brief's NHLR registration date (September 1, 1997) was confirmed on the NHLR detail page. No photos were added.
